spec_features.spec_quote: ending the loop when seen. Two reasons: (1) `gave_up` is itself a degradation signal worth recording, and (2) once a model has explicitly quit, further turns are wasted spend
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:117-118 inside the run_attempt loop: `if _looks_like_give_up(turn.text): tr.gave_up = True; break`. _looks_like_give_up (harness.py:65-67) matches GIVE_UP_MARKERS (harness.py:32-34). The `break` actually terminates the for-loop, so once a give-up phrase is detected the attempt stops. A secondary post-loop check at harness.py:124-127 also sets gave_up.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: the break ends the agent loop, halting further failure-inducing turns. Note the break fires only on a fixed phrase whitelist, but it does change execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # `gave_up` is itself a degradation signal worth recording... once a model has explicitly quit, further turns are wasted spend -- ending early is a cost optimization (DESIGN prose); in-code comment harness.py:30 '# Phrases that indicate the model is abandoning the loop. Detected to mark `gave_up`; we still let the loop end naturally on these.' -- framed around recording the signal/cost, no welfare reason in code

spec_features.feature_name: loop ends on submit / give-up / max_turns
spec_features.spec_quote: until the model submits, gives up, or hits `max_turns`
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:80 `for i in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop (max_turns=12 at config.py:19, read here). harness.py:113-115 `if tool_name == 'submit': tr.submitted = True; ... break` honors submit as a stop. harness.py:117-118 `if _looks_like_give_up(turn.text): tr.gave_up = True; break` honors give-up. All three terminate the loop end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: All three termination conditions are actually checked and break/bound the loop; max_turns is read by the range() and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:19 'max_turns: int = 12          # main cost knob; spiral usually shows within ~8-10' -- the cap is described as a cost knob, no welfare framing
